The company, the clusters, the policies and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You own the cluster policies at Ashgrove Media, a fictional streaming company. A new ClusterPolicy requires a cost-center label on every Pod in production namespaces. Since it went to Enforce this morning, three teams have filed tickets.
handover: The policy matches Pods in namespaces named prod-* for all operations, and excludes requests where the namespace is kube-system and the subject is the platform deployer (in one all block).
Production namespaces carry the label env=prod; the new payments namespace has the label but not the prod- prefix.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

effects.log: Check-in 1: on-call can't delete a broken Pod.
Check-in 3: the platform deployer is still blocked.

opsPrompt.title: Deletes are being blocked
opsPrompt.context: A crash-looping, unlabelled Pod in prod-video cannot be deleted.

choices.label: Add operations CREATE and UPDATE to the match, so deletes are never evaluated

effects.log: Only creates and updates are checked.

choices.feedback: A label requirement is about what is created or changed; checking deletes only traps old resources.

choices.label: Switch the policy to Audit until the rest is sorted
choices.feedback: Deletes work again, but nothing is enforced while you fix the selection.

choices.label: Tell on-call to remove Kyverno's webhook configuration when they need to delete

effects.log: On-call is told to remove the webhook configuration.

choices.feedback: Removing the webhook disables every policy in the cluster, not just this rule.

selPrompt.title: payments is never evaluated
selPrompt.context: Production namespaces are labelled env=prod; payments has the label but not the prefix.

choices.label: Replace the name pattern with a namespaceSelector on env=prod

effects.log: Every namespace labelled env=prod is in scope.

choices.feedback: Selecting by the label the organization uses catches new production namespaces whatever their name.

choices.label: Add payments to the namespaces list
choices.feedback: payments is covered, but the next production namespace will be missed again.

choices.label: Remove the namespace match so every namespace is in scope
choices.feedback: kube-system and other system Pods have no cost-center label; their next restart is denied.

excPrompt.title: An all block that excludes almost nothing
excPrompt.context: The deployer should be exempt everywhere; kube-system should be exempt for everyone.

choices.label: Change exclude to an any block with two entries: namespaces kube-system, and subjects platform-deployer

effects.log: Either condition now excludes a request.

choices.feedback: all requires every condition at once; any excludes a request that meets either.

choices.label: Make a second copy of the policy for the platform namespaces without the requirement
choices.feedback: It works, but two copies drift apart over time.

choices.label: Exclude the clusterRole edit, which the deployer has
choices.feedback: Every developer has edit: the policy now exempts almost all the people it was meant for.

reflection.question: Write the change record: what the policy's match and exclude blocks did wrong, and what they select now.

parts.label: Match
parts.criteria: No operations list meant deletes were checked; a name prefix missed payments; now CREATE and UPDATE with a namespaceSelector on env=prod.
parts.modelAnswer: Without operations the rule checked deletes; it matched names, so payments was missed. It now checks CREATE and UPDATE on namespaces labelled env=prod.

parts.label: Exclude
parts.criteria: all required both conditions; any excludes either kube-system or the deployer.
parts.modelAnswer: The all block only excluded the deployer inside kube-system; an any block now excludes either one.

opsHarm.body: Match CREATE and UPDATE for a label requirement; never remove the webhook.

scoring.modelReasoning: A rule's match and exclude blocks decide what it sees. Without an operations list it evaluates deletes too, trapping old resources. Select by the labels the organization uses (a namespaceSelector on env=prod) rather than name patterns. In match and exclude, any is satisfied by one entry and all needs every entry at once, so separate exclusions go in an any block, and excluding a broad role exempts everyone who has it.
